title: Implement capture-quiescence handshake and fuzz-driven replay validator for multi-stream CUDA graphs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Interleaved multi-stream decodes and cudaGraph capture/replay currently suffer intermittent divergence and rare corruption when prefill boundaries, kernel affinity changes, or KV-cache epoch shifts occur. Symptoms seen in production: transient garbled tokens after a replay fallback, rare OOMs during capture recapture, and head-of-line latency spikes when a warmup recapture blocks a hot stream.

Goal: Design and implement a lightweight capture-quiescence handshake protocol that establishes a deterministic capture window across concurrent decode streams, combined with a fuzz-driven replay validator and a kernel-fallback scoring table. The handshake should enable safe capture and recapture without heavy global locks, and the validator should detect non-deterministic replay outcomes in CI and stress runs.

Scope: runtime serving layer (CUDA graph capture manager, prefill coordinator), KV cache epoch alignment, kernel selection scoring, and CI fuzz harness. Excludes user-facing API changes.
acceptance_criteria: Handshaker protocol implemented: streams negotiate a capture-quiescent epoch before graph capture without introducing global mutexes
Replay validator harness that fuzzes prefill lengths, interleaved stream starts, and kernel affinity changes added to CI (nightly stress run)
Replay determinism failure rate under fuzzing reduced to <0.01% compared to current baseline
Kernel-fallback scoring table implemented and exercised: when preferred kernel unavailable, fallback produces identical outputs within numeric tolerance and logs a single deterministic decision path
No measurable p95 latency regression for steady-state decode (<= 3% change) on representative benchmarks
Integration test that reproduces a previously observed production divergence is fixed with the handshake protocol
technical_notes: Handshake design: each decode stream obtains a local quiescence token from CaptureManager; CaptureManager maintains minimal epoch counters per GPU and per-occupancy class. Token acquisition is optimistic; if token conflict detected, stream falls into staggered warmup rather than blocking capture.

KV epoch alignment: prefill routines will publish a prefill-epoch marker into KVCache metadata. During capture, the epoch marker is snapshotted and validated on replay. Mismatches trigger a safe recapture path that preserves committed KV state.

Kernel selection: implement kernel-scoring table keyed by <arch, seq_len_range, batch_size>. Score includes estimated latency, memory headroom, and numeric stability heuristics. Fallback path logs score deltas for post-mortem analysis.

Validator harness: fuzz inputs include stream interleaving patterns, random prefill token counts (1..max_prefill), simulated kernel failure modes (return code errors, out-of-memory), and forced scheduler preemption. The harness will compare golden output from single-stream reference runs to multi-stream replay outputs and record diffs with kernels and epochs annotated.

Observability: add structured logs for capture start/commit/abort, per-stream token counts at capture, chosen kernel id and score, KV epoch id, and replay diff hashes. Wire these into Console tracing and an alert when replay diffs exceed threshold in nightly runs.

CaptureManager handshake prototype merged behind feature flag
Fuzz-driven replay validator added to nightly CI pipeline
Stress run results analyzed and flaky cases triaged
Feature flag rollout plan prepared for canary and full rollout
comments: 2025-02-11 | Aisha Patel: Initial spike completed. Prototype handshake using optimistic epoch tokens avoids global lock but still had a 0.3% regression on p95 in microbenchmarks. Investigating batching edge-case when two streams attempt capture within same nanosecond window.

2025-02-13 | Liam Chen: Kernel-scoring table schema v0 implemented. Added telemetry for score deltas. Found that for seq_len 256 on A100s, fallback to smaller-warp fused attention produced slightly different fp16 rounding — added numeric-tolerance check to validator.

2025-02-15 | Martina Ruiz (Applied ML): Ran 24h fuzz harness. Repro rate for previously observed divergence dropped from ~0.12% to 0.006% under feature flag. Remaining failures concentrated where prefill crosses KV epoch boundary during capture commit.

2025-02-18 | QA: Added integration test that reproduces divergence using a 3-stream interleave pattern. Test currently flakes with feature-flag on in 1/500 runs; next step is to add snapshot validation at commit points.

2025-02-20 | Liam Chen: Opened PR #4821 for capture manager changes and PR #4823 for validator harness. Plan to enable nightly CI fuzz run and collect traces for any failures. Preparing canary rollout steps for runtime-1.21 if nightly is green for 72h.
